 Gillespie may soon be one of Spurs’ secret weapons
 Tre Torres , Graphic Artist 
 October 20, 2026 
 Sarah Quintanilla 
 After a 126-97 rout against the Sacramento Kings, the San Antonio Spurs’ preseason came to a harmonious close. While going 2-3 through five games, the record matters little, but the rookie class used the stage to flash real promise. Point guard Ja’Kobi Gillespie, the 22-year-old selected with the 42nd pick in June, used garbage time to hit three of four shots from behind the arc in the fourth quarter. Gillespie finished the game with 11 points in ten minutes and zero turnovers.
 While most of the new draft picks gave it their all for both Friday’s game and the entire preseason, few took better advantage than Gillespie. Gillespie’s athleticism shined as the rookie had an adept performance against the Utah Jazz last Monday, scoring 25 points, including 15 in the fourth quarter. Gillespie also had 13 points and four assists in last Wednesday’s matchup against the Phoenix Suns in a Spurs victory. Across five exhibition games, Gillespie averaged 12 points in 14 minutes per game, shooting an impressive 48.8% from the field and 50% from 3-point range. This is, of course, a very small sample size against varying opponents, but Gillespie deserves credit.
 Gillespie’s college resume explains why the poise at the next level is genuine. The rookie played at three different universities over four seasons, averaging 9.6 points per game at Belmont University in his freshman year and 17.2 for his sophomore year. Gillespie was a third-team All-Big Ten selection at the University of Maryland, leading the conference in 3-pointers. As a senior at the University of Tennessee, Gillespie averaged 18.4 points, 5.4 assists and a program record-breaking 79 steals in a season. Gillespie’s stats during his tenure at Tennessee were achieved with less efficiency, with 41% field goal percentage and 33.8% from three.
 Gillespie proved why scouts sought him in the draft: his ability to read screens, a calm and steady demeanor and quality ball protection. With two assists in 14 minutes, he averaged close to six in 36 minutes, which correlates with his numbers at Tennessee. The same goes for his steals, averaging one steal per 14 minutes.
 There is uncertainty regarding the rookie’s size. Measuring six feet tall with a reach of 6 foot 4 inches, Gillespie has been known to get out-muscled by larger opponents and does not possess an explosive first-step. The minutes Gillespie played during the preseason against bench players do not answer that question either; neither does his Summer League experience, where his shooting was off-target despite posting 14.6 points and 5.0 assists on average.
 “He’s a guy that in terms of what we’re looking for from every single person on our roster, the way that he’s guarding and competing, sharing the basketball, playing with pace, being aggressive, attacking, [is doing a good job],” coach Mitch Johnson stated . “He’s not perfect, but he’s playing with confidence and putting his energy in the right spots. The next thing you know, he has a lot of opportunities and advantageous spots that he finds himself in.”
 Gillespie’s role with the Spurs is indeterminate for now. With the guard-heavy roster boasting solid players like De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper and Jordan McLaughlin, Gillespie is already signed to a two-way contract with the Spurs and their developmental team, the Austin Spurs. The Spurs currently have an opening in their lineup, and the second unit that needs a point guard off the dribble would do well to utilize Gillespie. While opening night may not be Gillespie’s for now, the Spurs still have an open spot that could give him time to shine.

 Tre Torres , Graphic Artist 
 Tre Torres is a first-year UT San Antonio student majoring in architecture. Originally from the Round Rock area, he’s always sketching out stuff on anything that can be considered a canvas. Outside of The Paisano, he spends his free time playing and collecting Pokémon (especially the Trading Card Game), making mixtapes or cooking up his homemade pan-seared blackened chicken thighs with crispy potatoes and roasted broccoli recipe. 
 Sarah Quintanilla , Graphic Editor 
 Sarah (she/her) is a senior Fine Arts major at UTSA. She is an Industrial Designer and artist from Monterrey, Mexico. When she’s not researching obscure music history facts or making art, she enjoys watching movies, collecting cds, or finding new hobbies. This is her fifth semester at The Paisano and her second year serving as Graphic Editor.
